A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CreTok research, with matching core methods and identifiable corresponding experiments and figures. All supplied material is readable. V1 ends with references despite mentioning an appendix; v3 includes Appendices A–D, allowing comparison of what each PDF actually documents.

before.justification: V1 reports original generated images, PickScore and HPSv2 results in Table 1, and training-convergence results in Figure 7.

after.justification: V3 reports original generation experiments, quantitative comparisons, GPT-4o assessments, user-study rankings, and a loss-threshold analysis, including additional results in the appendices.

M1.justification: The learned token, frozen diffusion model, and CLIP similarity training remain. Section 3.2 revises the stated pair-order handling from randomizing the order in v1 to alternating positions and computing losses for both orders in v3. The loss threshold was already described in v1, so its explicit formulation does not establish a newly introduced component.

E1.justification: Animal/plant concept blending, concept-free and multi-concept generation, and the original style demonstrations remain. Appendix B.3 adds style and background conditions such as cubist painting, stained glass, mosaic, and cyberpunk scenes. The replacement of the test-pair selection is principally a protocol change within retained task coverage.

E2.justification: V3 adds BASS to Table 1's quantitative comparison, which previously included SD3, SD3.5, Kandinsky, and CreTok. The principal qualitative comparator set is retained. DiffMorpher and several MagicMix examples move from v1 Figure 4 to v3 Figure B.1; they are not removed.

E3.justification: Section 4 replaces the stated 100 test pairs with 27 pairs from BASS while retaining 200 training pairs. The reported learning rate changes from constant 0.0001 to an initial 0.01 with cosine scheduling; this does not establish whether experiments were rerun. V3 replaces HPSv2 with VQAScore and ImageReward alongside PickScore, and introduces a GPT-4o evaluation protocol.

E4.justification: V3 adds Section 6.2 and Figure 8, examining thresholds from 0.1 to 0.9 and selecting 0.5. The convergence curve and intermediate-generation examples in Figure 7 are retained. Appendix B.1 redisplays existing comparison examples rather than introducing a new robustness experiment.

E5.justification: V3 Tables 2 and 3 introduce plus/minus uncertainty values for GPT-4o scores and user-study rankings, whereas v1's quantitative table reports point estimates. The PDFs do not define these new uncertainty quantities or their estimation procedure. Neither version specifies repeated-training-run counts, seeds, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Table 1 replaces numerical results: for example, CreTok's PickScore changes from 21.9853 to 21.775 under revised reported settings, so this is not an established same-setting deterioration. V3 adds alignment, ImageReward, GPT-4o, user-ranking, and threshold results, and revises BASS generation time from 40 minutes to 40 seconds. Its new user-study results are internally inconsistent: Table 3 reports CreTok's mean rank as 1.9, while Table C.1's 27 pair means average about 2.49.

T1.justification: V3 Equation (3) explicitly defines the thresholded objective as 1 minus the minimum of cosine similarity and theta, and Equation (4) averages this objective. V1 only describes using a threshold without specifying its mathematical form. The other principal objectives remain equivalent, and neither version contains substantive theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: V3 drops v1's explicit priority claim of being the first method to redefine abstract semantics, particularly adjectives, and adds an explicit claim of superior text-image alignment. Universal token reuse, image-free concept blending, and style flexibility remain the central contributions. The term 'meta-creativity' largely reframes these retained capabilities.

C2.justification: V3 adds a specific interpretation of the threshold tradeoff: insufficient similarity produces separate objects, while excessive similarity favors one concept, motivating theta = 0.5. The introduction also develops the blue-banana example to distinguish ordinary out-of-distribution generation from combinatorial creativity. Earlier explanations of convergence and reference-image dependence remain.

D1.justification: Appendix A newly specifies the pooled 2048-dimensional CLIP conditioning vector on which the method operates. Appendices C and D provide the GPT-4o rubric, the 50-participant ranking procedure, study interface and stimuli, and the complete 200-pair training list. V3 also adds a prospective code-repository link. These substantially expand documentation without establishing that all underlying procedures changed.

R1.justification: V3 adds discussion of ATIH and references supporting VQAScore, ImageReward, GPT-based evaluation, and additional diffusion research, while dropping HPSv2 and some earlier creativity references. Positioning against ConceptLab, BASS, and personalization methods remains substantially intact, although the explicit first-method novelty claim is removed.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and substantial portions of the methods and results prose are rewritten around the semantic-understanding argument and 'meta-creativity.' Constraint/object prompts become restrictive/adaptive prompts. Dedicated evaluation subsections and Appendices A–D substantially expand the organization, beyond ordinary copyediting.

P2.justification: Figures 1 and 2 are redrawn, Figure 4 is reorganized with examples relocated to Figure B.1, and Figure 6 is reformatted. Table 1 is expanded, and new GPT-4o, user-study, dataset, threshold, and supplementary image displays are added. Figure 7 retains its underlying curve and images despite surrounding layout changes.

improvement.justification: V3 improves inspectability and reproducibility through explicit conditioning details, the training-pair list, evaluation prompts, and displayed user-study data. It also adds useful threshold evidence and broader evaluation beyond v1's preference proxies. However, the unexplained discrepancy between the user-study mean in Table 3 and the pair-level results in Table C.1, together with undefined uncertainty values, limits confidence in the empirical strengthening. The clearer specification and additional inspectable evidence provide a limited net improvement.
